item.text: Two cultures may divide the day differently because time is shaped not only by nature but also by social needs and traditions. Climate, work patterns, religious rituals, meal schedules, and political systems can make certain parts of the light–dark cycle more important. For example, one society might emphasize dawn because of farming, while another highlights midday because of markets or prayer. Thus, people experience the same cycle, but cultural activities give its periods different meanings and boundaries.
